Detect emerging variants across time points

Source: R/longitudinal.R
detectEmergingVariants.Rd

Identifies variants whose allele frequency crosses a threshold between consecutive time points within each host. A variant is considered emerging if it was below freqThreshold at one time point and increased by at least minIncrease at the next. Replicate samples taken at one time point are combined first: the variant's frequency there is the mean of the replicates' calls, so replicates never form an interval of their own and the result does not depend on the order of the columns. Intervals join the consecutive time points at which the variant has a call in the host; a time point without a call for it is passed over, since no call is not a frequency of 0, so a variant first called at a later time point is not reported.

Usage

detectEmergingVariants(
  whe,
  hostCol = "host_id",
  timeCol = "timepoint",
  freqThreshold = 0.05,
  minIncrease = 0.05,
  usePassedOnly = TRUE
)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment with longitudinal samples.

hostCol

Character scalar. Column name in colData for host identifier (default: "host_id"). Samples whose host is NA are left out, with a warning.

timeCol

Character scalar. Column name in colData for time point (default: "timepoint"), read as in trackFrequency: it is put in time order, and samples whose time point is NA are left out, with a warning.

freqThreshold

Numeric scalar. Frequency threshold for emergence (default: 0.05).

minIncrease

Numeric scalar. Minimum frequency increase between consecutive time points (default: 0.05).

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default), an interval is reported only when the later time point has a call that passed QC, and its frequency is the mean of those calls. The earlier time point is the mean of its passing calls too, or of all its calls when none passed: flagISNV fails a frequency below the filter's minFreq, and such a frequency is the low start that emergence is measured from. qc_from says which. Intervals are formed on every call before QC is applied, so a time point that failed QC, for example above maxFreq, is never passed over. With FALSE every call is used.

Value

A DataFrame with columns:

host_id

Host identifier.

variant_key

Variant identifier (chrom:pos:alt).

time_from

Earlier time point.

time_to

Later time point.

freq_from

Frequency at the earlier time point.

freq_to

Frequency at the later time point.

delta_freq

Change in frequency.

qc_from

Logical. Whether a call at the earlier time point passed QC (TRUE without a qcPass assay). A FALSE start failed QC, which a frequency below minFreq does by design; one that failed for low depth may be set aside.

One row is one interval, between two distinct time points. Rows are ordered by host, then by variant, each in order of first appearance in the object, then by time point.

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(100, 200), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("A", "C")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("T", "G")
freq <- matrix(c(0.02, 0.10, 0.12, 0.15), nrow = 2, ncol = 2)
whe <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = freq),
    rowRanges = gr,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("S1_t1", "S1_t2"),
        host_id = c("H1", "H1"),
        timepoint = c(1, 2)))
detectEmergingVariants(whe)
#> DataFrame with 1 row and 8 columns
#>       host_id variant_key time_from   time_to freq_from   freq_to delta_freq
#>   <character> <character> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric>  <numeric>
#> 1          H1  seg1:100:T         1         2      0.02      0.12        0.1
#>     qc_from
#>   <logical>
#> 1      TRUE
